title: I built a cyberpunk bullet-hell roguelike (solo, AI-assisted) — got keys to give away, mostly just want honest feedback
author: cybr1dtech
selftext:
Hey all,

I'm a solo dev (Bacondog Game Studio) and I recently put my game, Cyberpunk Neon Survivor, up on Steam. It's a top-down roguelike bullet-hell built in Godot 4 — the kind of thing where you start a run, dodge a screen full of pissed off cybernetic cats, stack some upgrades, and either die gloriously or get a little further than last time. The main character is a cybernetic beagle mix named Dunkin, who is, in real life, my actual dog and the studio mascot. He's earned it.

The honest pitch: it's meant to be a quick pick-up-and-go. Put on a synthwave or EDM track, do a couple of 5-minute runs to decompress after a busy day, and put it down. That's the whole vibe.

Happy to answer anything about the dev process. I'm also in the process of porting it over to iOS/Android so if you want in on the Android Beta - DM me you email and I'll add you to the tester group.

What I'm actually after: feedback. Does it feel good to play? Is it fun in those first few runs or does it drag? Anything that feels off? I'd take blunt over polite any day.

So — first folks to comment get a Steam key, no strings - I have 20 to give away. I'll DM it so it doesn't get scraped. If you end up enjoying it, an honest Steam review would mean a lot (I'm a brand-new release with basically none yet), but zero pressure — I mostly just want eyes on it and real reactions.

Thanks for reading. Dunkin says hi.
